nodes.label: GeneBench-Pro: Multi-Stage Scientific Reasoning Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark for AI agents performing realistic multi-stage quantitative analyses in genomics and translational biomedicine; 129 problems across 10 domains with 3-13 decision points each; uses simulated data to ensure identifiability and robust grading.

nodes.label: GeneBench-Pro Design Constraints
nodes.rationale: Eight primary constraints ensuring ground-truth identifiability, unique defensible answers, clear numerical separation, minimal viable prompts, robust QC, fully simulated problems, multi-stage inference, and ablation-supported workflow adjudication.

nodes.label: External Scientific Review Process
nodes.rationale: 82 of 129 problems reviewed by 11 domain experts; identified issues in estimand specification, method implementation, and workflow realism; led to prompt clarifications, data modifications, and complete redesigns.

nodes.label: DRX1 Carrier-Screening Residual Risk (Illustrative Problem)
nodes.rationale: Clinical genomics problem requiring carrier call identification, assay calibration, and residual risk computation; demonstrates multi-stage decision points including CNV/segdup discrimination, founder phase collapse, and full-roster standardization.

nodes.label: GeneBench-Pro Evaluation Results
nodes.rationale: GPT-5.6 Sol reaches 28.7% pass rate (31.5% with Pro); GPT-5.5 reaches 12.0%; Claude Opus 4.8 reaches 16.0%; models notice diagnostic clues but fail to propagate implications to downstream decisions.

nodes.label: Notice-Act Gap in Scientific Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Models identify diagnostic signals but fail to propagate implications to downstream analysis decisions; resembles expert-novice differences in scientific problem-solving where experts integrate observations into broader problem context.

nodes.label: Cascaded Decision Points in Scientific Analysis
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage problems with 3-13 decision points where incorrect upstream choices propagate downstream; enables measurement of whether agents navigate full inferential chains rather than isolated steps.

nodes.label: Simulated Data for Benchmark Construction
nodes.rationale: Enables precise control of complexity, difficulty, and diagnostic clues; ensures QC-sensitive decisions are robust to researcher-choice variation; guarantees graded endpoint is recoverable from agent-visible data.

nodes.label: Binary Grading Rationale
nodes.rationale: All-or-nothing grading reflects real-world scientific workflows where incorrect final answer despite partial correctness represents failure; collapses stage-level diagnostic evidence but maintains decision-relevance.

nodes.label: Model Reasoning Quality Assessment
nodes.rationale: Qualitative analysis of model-reported reasoning reveals consistent pattern: weaker models notice diagnostic clues but treat as local data cleaning rather than evidence for downstream method changes.
